### [Tips and Tricks](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/TipsAndTricks.md)

Tips and Tricks
Properties of functions
Perhaps surprisingly, FsCheck can generate random functions, Func and Actions. As a result, it can check properties of
functions. For example, we can check associativity of function composition as follows:
let associativity (x:int) (f:int->float,g:float->char,h:char->int) = ((f >> g) >> h) x = (f >> (g >> h)) x
Check.Quick associativity

Ok, passed 100 tests.
FsCheck can generate all functions with a target type that it can generate. In addition, the functions are pure and total -
the former means that if you give a generated function the same value as input, it will keep returning that same value as output,
no matter how many times you call it. The latter means that the function does not throw any exceptions and always terminates.
If a counter-example is found, function values will be displayed as <func>. However, FsCheck can show
you the generated function in more detail, if you ask it to generate a Function type, which has an embedded "real" function.
FsCheck can even shrink Functions. For example:
let mapRec (Fun f) (l:list<int>) =
  not l.IsEmpty ==>
      lazy (List.map f l = ((*f <|*) List.head l) :: List.map f (List.tail l))
Check.Quick mapRec

Falsifiable, after 1 test (0 shrinks) (16407225596337142791,9980540622768011905). 
Last step was invoked with size of 3 and seed of (15023365278686181315,17003805875138270743):
Original:
{ 0->1 }
[0]
with exception:
System.Exception: Expected true, got false.
The type Function<'a,'b> - here deconstructed using the single case active pattern Fun -
records a map of all the arguments it was called with, and the result it produced.
In your properties, you can extract the actual function by pattern matching as in the example.
Function is used to print the function, and also to shrink it.
Use pattern matching instead of forAll to use custom generators
To define a generator that generates a subset of the normal range of values for an existing type,
say all the even ints, it makes properties more readable if you define a single-case union
case, and register a generator for the new type:
type EvenInt = EvenInt of int with
  static member op_Explicit(EvenInt i) = i

type ArbitraryModifiers =
    static member EvenInt() = 
        ArbMap.defaults
        |> ArbMap.arbitrary<int> 
        |> Arb.filter (fun i -> i % 2 = 0) 
        |> Arb.convert EvenInt int
        
let ``generated even ints should be even`` (EvenInt i) = i % 2 = 0
Check.One(Config.Quick.WithArbitrary([typeof<ArbitraryModifiers>]), ``generated even ints should be even``)

Ok, passed 100 tests.
This example builds on the default int Arbitrary instance in three steps:

ArbMap.defaults |> ArbMap.arbitrary<int> retrieves the default instance.
Arb.filter keeps only even values, filtering both generated values and shrinks.
Arb.convert wraps the values in EvenInt, preserving the mapped shrink behavior.

The static member returns Arbitrary<EvenInt>. Passing its containing type to
Config.WithArbitrary registers it for this check; FsCheck discovers the instance from the member's return type.
It's now easy to define custom shrink functions as well.
FsCheck uses this pattern frequently, e.g. NonNegativeInt, PositiveInt, StringWithoutNullChars etc. The default
Arbitrary instances are available through ArbMap.defaults; for example,
ArbMap.defaults |> ArbMap.arbitrary<int> retrieves the default Arbitrary<int>.
Also, for these kinds of generators, the Arb.filter, Arb.convert and Arb.mapFilter functions will come in handy.
An equality comparison that prints the left and right sides of the equality
Properties commonly check for equality. If a test case fails, FsCheck prints the counterexample, but
sometimes it is useful to print the left and right side of the comparison, especially if you
do some complicated calculations with the generated arguments first. To make this easier, you can
define your own labelling equality combinator:
let (.=.) left right = left = right |> Prop.label (sprintf "%A = %A" left right)

let testCompare (i:int) (j:int) = 2*i+1  .=. 2*j-1
Check.Quick testCompare

Falsifiable, after 3 tests (3 shrinks) (5402073103309519350,8193260362427823847). 
Last step was invoked with size of 4 and seed of (276631440142415175,6520545709505150863).
Replay directly at failing step with (276631440142415175,6520545709505150863,4).
Label of failing property: 1 = -1
Original:
-3
-1
Shrunk:
0
0
with exception:
System.Exception: Expected true, got false.
Of course, you can do this for any operator or function that you often use.
Some ways to run FsCheck tests


By adding properties and generators to an fsx file in your project. It's easy to execute, just press 
ctrl-a and alt-enter, and the results are displayed in F# Interactive. Be careful when referencing dlls
that are built in your solution; Versions of F# Interactive earlier than 3.1.2 will lock those for the remainder of the session,
and you won't be able to build until you quit the session. One solution is to include the source files
instead of the dlls, but that makes the process slower. Useful for smaller projects. Difficult to debug though.


By making a separate console application. Easy to debug, and no annoying locks on assemblies. Your best option 
if you use only FsCheck for testing and your properties span multiple assemblies.


By using another unit testing framework. Useful if you have a mixed FsCheck/unit testing approach 
(some things are easier to check using unit tests, and vice versa), and you like a graphical runner.
Depending on what unit testing framework you use, you may get good integration with Visual Studio for free. Also have a look
at some of the existing integrations with test runners like Xunit.NET, NUnit, Fuchu.


Testing mutable types without using Command or StateMachine
For some relatively simple mutable types you might feel more comfortable just writing straightforward FsCheck properties without
using the Command or StateMachine API. This is certainly possible, but for shrinking FsCheck assumes that it can
re-execute the same test multiple times without the inputs changing. If you call methods or set properties on a generated object
that affect its state, this assumption does not hold and you'll see some weird results.
The simplest way to work around this is not to write a generator for your mutable object at all, but instead write an FsCheck property
that takes all the values necessary to construct the object, and then simply construct the object in the beginning of your test. For example, suppose we want to test
a mutable list:
let testMutableList =
    Prop.forAll (Arb.fromGen(Gen.choose (1,10))) (fun capacity -> 
        let underTest = new System.Collections.Generic.List<int>(capacity)
        Prop.forAll (ArbMap.defaults |> ArbMap.arbitrary<int[]>) (fun itemsToAdd ->
            underTest.AddRange(itemsToAdd)
            underTest.Count = itemsToAdd.Length))

Prop.ForAll(Gen.Choose(1, 10).ToArbitrary(), ArbMap.Default.ArbFor<int[]>(),(capacity, itemsToAdd) => {
    var underTest = new List<int>(capacity);
    underTest.AddRange(itemsToAdd);
    return underTest.Count == itemsToAdd.Length;
})
.QuickCheck();
This works, as a bonus you get shrinking for free.
If you do want to write a generator for your mutable type, this can be made to work but if
you mutate a generated object during a test, either:

Disable shrinking, typically by wrapping all types into DontShrink; or
Clone or otherwise 'reset' the generated mutable object at the beginning or end of every test.

Replaying a failed test
When you have a failed test, it's often useful for debugging to be able to replay exactly those inputs. For this reason, FsCheck displays the
seed of its pseudo-random number generator when a test fails. Look for the bit of text that looks like: (StdGen (1145655947,296144285)).
To replay this test, which should have the exact same output, use the Replay field on Config:
Check.One(Config.Quick.WithReplay(1145655947UL,296144285UL), fun x -> abs x >= 0)

In C#:
Prop.ForAll((int x) => Math.Abs(x) >= 0)
    .Check(Config.Quick.WithReplay(1145655947UL, 296144285UL));
Checking properties in parallel
FsCheck can evaluate properties in parallel.
This feature may be useful to speed-up your cpu-heavy properties and custom arbitraries.
Also this is invaluable for running asynchronous propertiess, i.e. when you are doing asynchronous IO inside prop.
Don't forget to wrap your property in Task or Async in that case.
To run a property in parallel, use the ParallelRunConfig field on Config:
Check.One(
    Config.Quick.WithParallelRunConfig({ MaxDegreeOfParallelism = System.Environment.ProcessorCount }),
     fun x -> abs x >= 0
)

System.Environment.ProcessorCount is a good default for cpu-bound work.
For io-bound work it's usually enough to set ParallelRunConfig to 1.
Check.One(
    Config.Verbose.WithParallelRunConfig({ MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 1 } ),
    fun (x:int) -> 
        async { 
            do! Async.Sleep (abs x)
            return true
        }
)

### [Arbitrary<'T>.Shrinker](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-arbitrary-1.html#Shrinker)

Arbitrary<'T>.Shrinker 
Shrinker 
Returns a sequence of the immediate shrinks of the given value. The immediate shrinks should not include
doubles or the given value itself. The default implementation returns the empty sequence (i.e. no shrinking).

### [DoNotSize<'a>](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-donotsize-1.html)

DoNotSize<'a> 
Whereas most types are restricted by a size that grows
as the test gets further, by applying this type the underlying
type will ignore this size and always generate from the full range.
Note that this only makes a difference for types that have a range -
currently integer types, TimeSpan and Decimal have DoNotSize Arbitrary instances.
This is typically (and at least currently) only applicable for value types
that are comparable, hence the type constraints. 
DoNotSize<'a>.Unwrap 
Unwrap 
DoNotSize<'a>.DoNotSize 
DoNotSize

### [DoNotSize<'a>.Unwrap](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-donotsize-1.html#Unwrap)

DoNotSize

### [Rnd.``.ctor``](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-rnd.html#``.ctor``)

Rnd.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
 Create a new Rnd value with the specified seed value and the 'golden' gamma.

### [Rnd.``.ctor``](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-rnd.html#``.ctor``)

Rnd.``.ctor`` 
``.ctor`` 
 Create a new random number generator with the given seed and gamma.
 Useful to faithfully reproduce a sequence or part of it. gamma must be odd,
 or this throws invalid argument exception. For good pseudo-random properties,
 please only use seeds and gamma that were generated as part of a sequence
 started with the default create function.

### [Rnd.Seed](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-rnd.html#Seed)

Rnd.Seed 
Seed 
 Seed value for the random number generator.

### [Rnd.Gamma](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-rnd.html#Gamma)

Rnd.Gamma 
Gamma 
 An odd integer

### [Operation<'Actual, 'Model>](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-experimental-operation-2.html)

Operation<'Actual, 'Model> 
An operation describes pre and post conditions and the model for a single operation under test.
The post-conditions are the invariants that will be checked; when these do not hold the test fails.

### [Operation<'Actual, 'Model>.Check](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-experimental-operation-2.html#Check)

Operation<'Actual, 'Model>.Check 
Check 
Executes the command on the object under test, and returns a property that must hold.
This property typically compares the state of the model with the state of the object after
execution of the command.

### [Operation<'Actual, 'Model>.Pre](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-experimental-operation-2.html#Pre)

Operation<'Actual, 'Model>.Pre 
Pre 
Optional precondition for execution of the command. When this does not hold, the test continues
but the command is not executed.

### [Operation<'Actual, 'Model>.Run](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-experimental-operation-2.html#Run)

Operation<'Actual, 'Model>.Run 
Run 
Executes the command on the model of the object.

### [Setup<'Actual, 'Model>.Actual](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-experimental-setup-2.html#Actual)

Setup<'Actual, 'Model>.Actual 
Actual 
Randomly generate the initial state of the actual object. Should still correspond to the 
initial state of model object; so you should only randomly generate parameters to the instance
that don't affect the model.
Note:make sure that each value is truly a new instance if the commands change the state
of the object. Gen.connstant in particular is a bad idea - use Gen.fresh instead.

### [Setup<'Actual, 'Model>.Model](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-experimental-setup-2.html#Model)

Setup<'Actual, 'Model>.Model 
Model 
Initial state of model object. Must correspond to initial state of actual object.

fromGen

Arb.fromGenShrink 
fromGenShrink

### [Arb.convert](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#convert)

Arb.convert 
convert 
 Construct an Arbitrary instance for a type that can be mapped to and from another type (e.g. a wrapper),
 based on a Arbitrary instance for the source type and two mapping functions.

### [Arb.filter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#filter)

Arb.filter 
filter 
 Return an Arbitrary instance that is a filtered version of an existing arbitrary instance.
 The generator uses Gen.where, and the shrinks are filtered using Seq.filter with the given predicate.

### [Arb.mapFilter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#mapFilter)

Arb.mapFilter 
mapFilter 
 Return an Arbitrary instance that is a mapped and filtered version of an existing arbitrary instance.
 The generator uses Gen.map with the given mapper and then Gen.where with the given predicate,
 and the shrinks are filtered using Seq.filter with the given predicate.
 This is sometimes useful if using just a filter would reduce the chance of getting a good value
 from the generator - and you can map the value instead. E.g. PositiveInt.

### [Arb.zip](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#zip)

Arb.zip 
zip 
 Generates 2-tuples.

### [Arb.array](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#array)

Arb.array 
array 
 Generates one-dimensional arrays. 
 The length of the generated array is between 0 and size.
 The sum of the sizes of the elements is equal to the size of the generated array.

### [Arb.option](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#option)

Arb.option 
option 
 Generates option values that are None 1/8 of the time.

### [Arb.nullable](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#nullable)

Arb.nullable 
nullable 
 Generates nullable values that are null 1/8 of the time.

### [Arb.nullableRef](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#nullableRef)

Arb.nullableRef 
nullableRef 
 Generates reference values that are null 1/8 of the time.

### [Arb.list](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#list)

Arb.list 
list 
 Generates FSharp.Core list<'T> values. 
 The length of the generated list is between 0 and size. 
 The sum of the sizes of the elements is equal to the size of the generated list.

### [Arb.pureFunction](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#pureFunction)

Arb.pureFunction 
pureFunction 
 Generates pure functions that produce the given output values 'U. 
 There is no shrinking for functions.

### [Arb.throwingFunction](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#throwingFunction)

Arb.throwingFunction 
throwingFunction 
 Generates F# function values that generate an instance of the function result type about half the time. The other 
 times it generate one of the given exceptions.

### [Arb.set](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#set)

Arb.set 
set 
 Generates Set<'T> values.

### [Arb.mapKV](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arb.html#mapKV)

Arb.mapKV 
mapKV 
 Generates Map<TKey,TValue> values.
 Not named `map` because that has other meanings.

### [ArbMap.defaults](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arbmap.html#defaults)

ArbMap.defaults 
defaults

### [ArbMap.mergeWithType](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arbmap.html#mergeWithType)

ArbMap.mergeWithType 
mergeWithType 
 Return a new Type to Arbitrary map that merges the existing map with new Arbitrary<'T> instances
 discovered on the given Type. See mergeWith<'TArb> for more info on what the shape of instancesType can be.

### [ArbMap.mergeWith](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-arbmap.html#mergeWith)

ArbMap.mergeWith 
mergeWith 
 Return a new Type to Arbitrary map that merges the existing map with new Arbitrary<'T> instances
 discovered on the given type argument 'TArb.
 The new Arbitrary instances take precedence over the ones for the same type
 in the existing map.

 instancesType should have static methods or properties that return Arbitrary<'T>
 instances. The methods or properties can have any name, and there can be any number of them.

 A method may return Arbitrary instances for generic types, e.g. Arbitrary<KeyValuePair<'K,'V>>.
 In that case, the implementation needs to obtain an Arbitrary<'Key> and Arbitrary<'Value> - it can declare
 parameters of type Arbitrary<'T> to obtain them. Arbitrary instance of the correct type are automatically
 injected on construction of a particular type.

mergeFactory 
 Return a new Type to Arbitrary map that merges the existing map with the Arbitrary<'T> returned by the given function.

### [Gen.delay](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#delay)

Gen.delay 
delay 
 Create a generator by deferring its construction until a value is generated.

### [Gen.constant](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#constant)

Gen.constant 
constant 
 Always generate the same given value. See also fresh.

### [Gen.map](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#map)

Gen.map 
map 
 Create a new generator by applying f to each value in the given generator.

### [Gen.fresh](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#fresh)

Gen.fresh 
fresh 
 Generate fresh instances by calling create every time the generator 
 generates a new value. Useful for generating new instances of mutable
 objects.
 See also constant.

### [Gen.apply](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#apply)

Gen.apply 
apply 
 Apply the functions f from the first generator to the values from the second generator pairwise,
 yielding a new generator that generates the results.

### [Gen.bind](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#bind)

Gen.bind 
bind 
 Creates a new generator that generates values from the source generator, 
 applies the function k to them, and generates values from the resulting generator.

map2 
 Create a new generator by applying f to each value in the given generators.

sample

elements 
Build a generator that randomly generates one of the values in the given non-empty, finite seq.

### [Gen.growingElements](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#growingElements)

Gen.growingElements 
growingElements 
Build a generator that takes a non-empty sequence and randomly generates
one of the values among an initial segment of that sequence. The size of
this initial segment increases with the size parameter. Essentially this
generator is Gen.elements but taking also the size into account.

### [Gen.oneof](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#oneof)

Gen.oneof 
oneof 
Build a generator that generates a value from one of the generators in the given non-empty seq, with
equal probability.

### [Gen.frequency](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#frequency)

Gen.frequency 
frequency 

 Build a generator that generates a value from one of the generators in the given non-empty seq, with
 given probabilities. The sum of the probabilities must be larger than zero.

### [Gen.tryWhere](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#tryWhere)

Gen.tryWhere 
tryWhere 
Tries to generate a value that satisfies a predicate. This function 'gives up' by generating None
if the given original generator did not generate any values that satisfied the predicate, after trying to
get values by increasing its size.

The `tryWhere` function is also aliased as `tryFilter`. These two functions are identical, but co-exist
so that you can choose the word that makes your code most readable in your given context.

### [Gen.tryFilter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#tryFilter)

Gen.tryFilter 
tryFilter 
Tries to generate a value that satisfies a predicate. This function 'gives up' by generating None
if the given original generator did not generate any values that satisfied the predicate, after trying to
get values by increasing its size.

The `tryFilter` function is an alias for the `tryWhere` function. These two functions are identical, but co-exist
so that you can choose the word that makes your code most readable in your given context.

### [Gen.where](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#where)

Gen.where 
where 
Generates a value that satisfies a predicate. Contrary to tryWhere, this function keeps re-trying
by increasing the size of the original generator ad infinitum.  Make sure there is a high probability that 
the predicate is satisfied.

The `where` function is also aliased as `filter`. These two functions are identical, but co-exist
so that you can choose the word that makes your code most readable in your given context.

### [Gen.filter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#filter)

Gen.filter 
filter 
Generates a value that satisfies a predicate. Contrary to tryFilter, this function keeps re-trying
by increasing the size of the original generator ad infinitum.  Make sure there is a high probability that 
the predicate is satisfied.

The `filter` function is an alias for the `where` function. These two functions are identical, but co-exist
so that you can choose the word that makes your code most readable in your given context.

### [Gen.tryPick](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#tryPick)

Gen.tryPick 
tryPick 
Tries to apply the given chooser function to successive values generated by the given generator, 
returning the first result where the function returns Some(x). This function 'gives up' by generating None
if the given original generator did not generate any values for which the chooser function returned Some(x),
after trying to get values by increasing its size.

### [Gen.pick](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#pick)

Gen.pick 
pick 
Applies the given chooser function to successive values generated by the given generator, 
returning the first result where the function returns Some(x). Contrary to tryPick, this function 
keeps re-trying by increasing the size of the original generator ad infinitum. Make sure there is 
a high probability that the chooser function returns Some for some values.

### [Gen.shuffle](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#shuffle)

Gen.shuffle 
shuffle 
Generates random permutations of the given sequence.

### [Gen.piles](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#piles)

Gen.piles 
piles 
 Generates random arrays of given length where the sum of
 all elements equals the given sum.

### [Gen.subListOf](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-gen.html#subListOf)

Gen.subListOf 
subListOf 
 Generates sublists of the given seq. For a given list of length n,

### [Prop](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html)

Prop 
Combinators to build properties, which define the property to be tested, with some
convenience methods to investigate the generated arguments and any found counter-examples. 
Prop.forAll 
forAll 
Prop.given 
given 
Prop.filter 
filter 
Prop.throws 
throws 
Prop.classify 
classify 
Prop.trivial 
trivial 
Prop.collect 
collect 
Prop.label 
label 
Prop.ofTestable 
ofTestable 
Prop.discard 
discard

### [Prop.forAll](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#forAll)

Prop.forAll 
forAll 
Quantified property combinator. Provide a custom test data generator to a property.

### [Prop.given](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#given)

Prop.given 
given 
Depending on the condition, return the first testable if true and the second if false.

### [Prop.filter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#filter)

Prop.filter 
filter 
Conditional property combinator. Resulting property holds if the given property holds whenever the condition does. See also operator:  'assertion ==> property'

### [Prop.throws](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#throws)

Prop.throws 
throws 
Expect exception 't when executing p. So, results in success if an exception of the given type is thrown, 
and a failure otherwise.

### [Prop.classify](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#classify)

Prop.classify 
classify 
Classify test cases. Test cases satisfying the condition are assigned the classification given.

### [Prop.trivial](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#trivial)

Prop.trivial 
trivial 
Count trivial cases. Test cases for which the condition is True are classified as trivial.

### [Prop.collect](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#collect)

Prop.collect 
collect 
Collect data values. The argument of collect is evaluated in each test case, 
and the distribution of values is reported, using sprintf "%A".

### [Prop.label](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#label)

Prop.label 
label 
Add the given label to the property. The labels of a failing sub-property are displayed when it fails.

### [Prop.ofTestable](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#ofTestable)

Prop.ofTestable 
ofTestable 
 Turns a testable type into a property. Testables are unit, Boolean, Lazy testables, Gen testables,
 Async testables, Task testables, and functions from a type for which a generator is known to a testable.

### [Prop.discard](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-prop.html#discard)

Prop.discard 
discard

### [PropOperators](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-propoperators.html)

PropOperators 
Operators for Prop.

(==>)

(.&.)

### [PropOperators.(==>)](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-propoperators.html#(==>))

PropOperators.(==>) 
(==>) 
Conditional property combinator. Resulting property holds if the property after ==> holds whenever the condition does.

### [PropOperators.(.&.)](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-propoperators.html#(.&.))

PropOperators.(.&.) 
(.&.) 
Construct a property that succeeds if both succeed. (cfr 'and')

### [PropOperators.(.|.)](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fsharp-propoperators.html#(.|.))

PropOperators.(.|.) 
(.|.) 
Construct a property that fails if both fail. (cfr 'or')

### [Arb.Array](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#Array)

Arb.Array 
Array 
 Generates one-dimensional arrays. 
 The length of the generated array is between 0 and size.
 The sum of the sizes of the elements is equal to the size of the generated array.

### [Arb.Convert](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#Convert)

Arb.Convert 
Convert 
Construct an Arbitrary instance for a type that can be mapped to and from another type (e.g. a wrapper),
based on a Arbitrary instance for the source type and two mapping functions.

### [Arb.Filter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#Filter)

Arb.Filter 
Filter 
 Return an Arbitrary instance that is a filtered version of an existing arbitrary instance.
 The generator uses Gen.where, and the shrinks are filtered using Seq.filter with the given predicate.

### [Arb.From](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#From)

Arb.From 
From 
 Construct an Arbitrary instance from a generator and shrinker.

### [Arb.From](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#From)

Arb.From 
From 
 Construct an Arbitrary instance from a generator.
 Shrink is not supported for this type.

### [Arb.MapFilter](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#MapFilter)

Arb.MapFilter 
MapFilter 
<pre> Return an Arbitrary instance that is a mapped and filtered version of an existing arbitrary instance.
 The generator uses Gen.map with the given mapper and then Gen.where with the given predicate, 
 and the shrinks are filtered using Seq.filter with the given predicate.
This is sometimes useful if using just a filter would reduce the chance of getting a good value
from the generator - and you can map the value instead. E.g. PositiveInt.</pre>

### [Arb.Nullable](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-fluent-arb.html#Nullable)

Arb.Nullable 
Nullable 
 Generates nullable values that are null 1/8 of the time.

GrowingElements

 one of the values among an initial segment of that array. The size of
 this initial segment increases with the size parameter. Essentially this
 generator is Gen.Elements but taking also the size into account.

### [Shrink<'T>](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-internals-shrink-1.html)

Shrink<'T> 
 Shrink<T> keeps a value and the possible shrinks for that value in an n-ary tree.
 This tree is explored by the test runner to find a smaller value of a counter-example.

### [PropertyAttribute.Arbitrary](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#Arbitrary)

PropertyAttribute.Arbitrary 
Arbitrary 
The Arbitrary instances to use for this test method. The Arbitrary instances
are merged in back to front order i.e. instances for the same generated type
at the front of the array will override those at the back.

### [PropertyAttribute.StartSize](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#StartSize)

PropertyAttribute.StartSize 
StartSize 
The size to use for the first test.

### [PropertyAttribute.MaxTest](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#MaxTest)

PropertyAttribute.MaxTest 
MaxTest 
The maximum number of tests that are run.

### [PropertyAttribute.EndSize](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#EndSize)

PropertyAttribute.EndSize 
EndSize 
The size to use for the last test, when all the tests are passing. The size increases linearly between Start- and EndSize.

### [PropertyAttribute.Replay](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#Replay)

PropertyAttribute.Replay 
Replay 
If set, the seed to use to start testing. Allows reproduction of previous runs. You can just paste
the tuple from the output window, e.g. 12344,12312 or (123,123).

### [PropertyAttribute.QuietOnSuccess](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#QuietOnSuccess)

PropertyAttribute.QuietOnSuccess 
QuietOnSuccess 
If set, suppresses the output from the test if the test is successful. This can be useful when running tests
with TestDriven.net, because TestDriven.net pops up the Output window in Visual Studio if a test fails; thus,
when conditioned to that behaviour, it's always a bit jarring to receive output from passing tests.
The default is false, which means that FsCheck will also output test results on success, but if set to true,
FsCheck will suppress output in the case of a passing test. This setting doesn't affect the behaviour in case of
test failures.

### [PropertyAttribute.MaxFail](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#MaxFail)

PropertyAttribute.MaxFail 
MaxFail 
The maximum number of tests where values are rejected, e.g. as the result of ==>

### [PropertyAttribute.Verbose](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#Verbose)

PropertyAttribute.Verbose 
Verbose 
Output all generated arguments.

### [PropertyAttribute.Parallelism](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-nunit-propertyattribute.html#Parallelism)

PropertyAttribute.Parallelism 
Parallelism 
If set, run tests in parallel. Useful for Task/async related work and heavy number crunching
Environment.ProcessorCount have been found to be useful default.

### [PropertyAttribute.EndSize](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute.html#EndSize)

PropertyAttribute.EndSize 
EndSize

### [PropertyAttribute.Replay](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute.html#Replay)

PropertyAttribute.Replay 
Replay 
If set, the seed to use to start testing. Allows reproduction of previous runs. You can just paste
the tuple from the output window, e.g. 12344,12312 or (123,123).
Additionally, you can also specify a start size as the third parameter, e.g. 12344,12312,10 or (123,123,10).

### [PropertyAttribute.QuietOnSuccess](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute.html#QuietOnSuccess)

PropertyAttribute.QuietOnSuccess 
QuietOnSuccess 
If set, suppresses the output from the test if the test is successful. This can be useful when running tests
with TestDriven.net, because TestDriven.net pops up the Output window in Visual Studio if a test fails; thus,
when conditioned to that behaviour, it's always a bit jarring to receive output from passing tests.
The default is false, which means that FsCheck will also output test results on success, but if set to true,
FsCheck will suppress output in the case of a passing test. This setting doesn't affect the behaviour in case of
test failures.

### [PropertyAttribute.Verbose](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute.html#Verbose)

PropertyAttribute.Verbose 
Verbose 
Output all generated arguments.

### [PropertyAttribute.Parallelism](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute.html#Parallelism)

PropertyAttribute.Parallelism 
Parallelism 
If set, run tests in parallel. Useful for Task/async related work and heavy number crunching
Environment.ProcessorCount have been found to be useful default.

### [PropertyAttribute.Arbitrary](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#Arbitrary)

PropertyAttribute.Arbitrary 
Arbitrary 
The Arbitrary instances to use for this test method. The Arbitrary instances
are merged in back to front order i.e. instances for the same generated type
at the front of the array will override those at the back.

### [PropertyAttribute.StartSize](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#StartSize)

PropertyAttribute.StartSize 
StartSize 
The size to use for the first test.

### [PropertyAttribute.MaxTest](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#MaxTest)

PropertyAttribute.MaxTest 
MaxTest 
The maximum number of tests that are run.

### [PropertyAttribute.MaxRejected](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#MaxRejected)

PropertyAttribute.MaxRejected 
MaxRejected 
The maximum number of tests where values are rejected, e.g. as the result of ==>

### [PropertyAttribute.EndSize](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#EndSize)

PropertyAttribute.EndSize 
EndSize 
The size to use for the last test, when all the tests are passing. The size increases linearly between Start- and EndSize.

### [PropertyAttribute.Replay](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#Replay)

PropertyAttribute.Replay 
Replay 
If set, the seed to use to start testing. Allows reproduction of previous runs. You can just paste
the tuple from the output window, e.g. 12344,12312 or (123,123).
Additionally, you can also specify a start size as the third parameter, e.g. 12344,12312,10 or (123,123,10).

### [PropertyAttribute.QuietOnSuccess](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#QuietOnSuccess)

PropertyAttribute.QuietOnSuccess 
QuietOnSuccess 
If set, suppresses the output from the test if the test is successful. This can be useful when running tests
with TestDriven.net, because TestDriven.net pops up the Output window in Visual Studio if a test fails; thus,
when conditioned to that behaviour, it's always a bit jarring to receive output from passing tests.
The default is false, which means that FsCheck will also output test results on success, but if set to true,
FsCheck will suppress output in the case of a passing test. This setting doesn't affect the behaviour in case of
test failures.

### [PropertyAttribute.Verbose](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#Verbose)

PropertyAttribute.Verbose 
Verbose 
Output all generated arguments.

### [PropertyAttribute.Parallelism](https://fscheck.github.io/FsCheck/reference/fscheck-xunit-propertyattribute-0.html#Parallelism)

PropertyAttribute.Parallelism 
Parallelism 
If set, run tests in parallel. Useful for Task/async related work and heavy number crunching
Environment.ProcessorCount have been found to be useful default.
